Judgment

By this judgment this Tribunal shall decide the petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- in respect of injuries sustained by her in the Road Traffic Accident.

2. It is the case of the petitioner that, on 23.01.2025 at about 03.00 to 03.05 pm petitioner was crossing the road carefully by observing traffic rules on Bellary Main road, near Palace Guttahalli,
Bus Stop in the lane of Zebra crossing from East towards West side, at that time driver of one Car bearing Reg. No.KA-04-ND-8844 came from Mekhri circle towards Bengaluru City in rash and negligent manner without observing pedestrians, dashed to petitioner.
As a result petitioner fell down and sustained injury to her head, right hand and other parts of the body.
She was shifted to MS Ramaiah Hospital Mathikere and first aid treatment was given, then she was shifted to Kanva Hospital for further treatment.
She was admitted there aa inpatient from 23.01.2025 to 26.01.2025.
she (SCCH-12) 3 MVC. No.1353/2025 has sustained injuries of right humerus middle third fracture with radial nerve Palsy and she underwent operation.
She has spent Rs.5 lakhs towards medical and other incidental expenses.
3. Prior to accident petitioner was hale and healthy, she was doing house hold work and professional ladies Tailor and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
Due to accidental injuries she is unable to continue the work and sustained permanent disability.
That accident is caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the Car by its driver.

Hence, Sadashivanagar traffic police have registered the criminal case in Cr.No.21/25 against the Car driver for the offence punishable under sec.281, 125(b)
of BNS.
1st respondent is the RC Owner and 2nd respondent is insurer of the car.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
On all these grounds, she prayed to allow the petition and award compensation.
4. On issuance of notice, respondent No.1 owner of car is served.
He appeared through his counsel and contested the case.
In his written statement he contended that petition is not maintainable and the claim of compensation is exorbitant without any reasons.
That in collusion with the jurisdictional Police, false case is filed against this respondent with malafide intention to get huge compensation.
The driver of Innova Car by name Channappa Huballi was having valid driving licence as on the date of accident to drive the said vehicle and the vehicle was insured with respondent no.2.
He was driving the vehicle by (SCCH-12) 4 MVC. No.1353/2025 following lane discipline and traffic rules.
Further petitioner without following traffic rules and also there was no zebra crossing, was crossing the road in negligent manner.
Therefore if the court comes to the conclusion that there is liability of 1st respondent, the 2nd respondent insurance company has to indemnify the insured and pay compensation to petitioner.
On all these grounds he prayed to dismiss the petition.

sentences.text: The 2nd respondent insurance company has filed written statement contending that petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
That vehicle No. KA-04-ND-8844 was insured with this respondent, but the liability is subjected to terms and conditions of the policy.
The protection under Section 149(2) of the MV Act is sought.
That petitioner has not approached this court with clean hands and the complaint has been lodged against the insured vehicle driver, twisting the facts for the purpose of gaining compensation.
The age, occupation, income and permanent disability alleged by the petitioner all are denied.
The driver of the said vehicle was driving the same in a cautious manner.
But accident occurred due to sole negligence of petitioner.

Compliance of Section 158(6)
and 1349 (c) of MV Act are disputed.
That driver had not got valid driving licence to drive the class of vehicle.
Therefore, this respondent is not liable to pay compensation to petitioner.
On all these grounds, respondent no. 2 prayed to reject the petition.

2 . Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so by whom and what is the quantum?

In her chief examination, she has produced Exhibit P1-15 documents.
One Sri.Manith Kumar .K, who is Medical Record Officer of Kanva Hospital got examined as PW2 and through him Exhibit P16 to 19 documents are marked.

On the other hand, 1st respondent owner of the opponent car got examined as RW.1 and through him Ex.R1 to R5 documents are marked.
2nd respondent insurance company has not led any evidence and respondent side evidence is closed.

On taking into consideration the oral and documentary evidence placed before this Tribunal and arguments of both sides, my findings to the above issues as under:-
 Issue No.1: Partly in the Affirmative,
 Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3: As per final order,
 for the following;
 REASONS 10. ISSUE No.1: It is the case of petitioner that she sustained accidental injuries due to rash and negligent driving of the car bearing no. KA-04-ND-8844.
To prove her case she herself entered witness box and got examined as PW1.
She has relied upon crime records in support of her claim and to show the accidental injuries she relied upon medical records.

On perusal of those documents it can be seen that Petitioner herself is first informant and on the next day of the accident the first information is registered by Sadashiva Nagara traffic police in Crime No.21/2025 against the driver of aforesaid car.
11.
In the first information she has mentioned the statement which she has pleaded in the petition.
The spot panchanamma was conducted which shows it is main road, in front of bus stop accident has taken place.
The width of the road is 40 feet wide (SCCH-12) 7 MVC. No.1353/2025 tar road.
The spot sketch is produced at Exhibit P4, which shows accident has occurred in the middle of the road towards Bengaluru City, wherein the pedestrian petitioner has crossed almost middle of the road.
The time of the accident is 03.00 p.m. which means there is no dispute as to visibility of the pedestrians or vehicles on the road.
In the answer to IMV notice, owner of the opponent car stated that his vehicle driver has caused accident and Crime No. 21/2025 is registered against him.
As per the IMV report, the car got front side damages and it is opined that, there was no mechanical defects in the vehicle.
Further as per the wound certificate petitioner was admitted to hospital on 23.01.2025 with the history of RTA and she has sustained grievous injury of fracture of right numerous
In the final report, it is mentioned that, driver of opponent car was rash and negligent in driving and offence under Section 281, 125(b) of BNS is registered against him.
12. On the basis of these documents, it can be seen that driver of car was rash and negligent in driving the vehicle.
The driver of the car or the owner have not challenged the final report.
But the owner of the car got examined as RW.1 and in his evidence he stated that his driver was not negligent in driving the vehicle.
It is necessary to notice that owner was not the driver of the car at the time of accident.
It was some other person by name.
Channappa C. Huballi.
Therefore, 1st respondent is not eye witness to the incident and his evidence is only on the basis of documents or on the basis of say of his driver.

However, he has produced his RC card, driving license of the driver,
copy of insurance and his own Aadhar card at (SCCH-12) 8 MVC. No.1353/2025 Exhibit R1 to R4.
But no independent witnesses are examined by the 1st respondent to prove his claim that petitioner herself is sole negligent.
13. In the cross-examination of PW1, it is brought out that she has not observed whether there is zebra crossing at that spot.

She has stated that other three persons went ahead of her to cross the Prathibha B C vs Xavier Kurian on 28 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175591565/
4 road and behind them she also went.

sentences.text: She has not observed there is any sky walk near the said road.
She has denied that though there was sky walk, without using the same, she tried to cross the road where there was no zebra crossing.
She admitted that car driver took her to hospital and arranged for treatment.
It is necessary to notice that petitioner who was trying to cross the road has not observed the skywalk nearby.
The spot sketch produced by the petitioner shows that there is sky walk very near to the bus stop, which is specifically made for pedestrians to cross from one side to other side of the road.
But without observing the same, she took the road and tried to cross it, which is also one of the reasons for accident.
Therefore in the opinion of this Court, the petitioner has also contributed to the accident to some extent.
In that view of the matter this Tribunal is of the opinion that contribution of petitioner to the accident is at 10% and contribution of the opponent car driver is at 90%.
Accordingly, this issue is answered Partly in the affirmative.
14. ISSUE No.2:
In view of above reasons, petitioner is entitled for compensation for the accidental injuries sustained by her in the road traffic accident.

Since the 2nd respondent has issued (SCCH-12) 9 MVC. No.1353/2025 the policy to offending vehicle and it was valid as on the date of accident, hence it has to indemnify the insured and pay compensation to petitioner for the portion of negligence of driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-ND-8844.
15.
To prove her age, petitioner has produced her aadhaar card at Ex.P.11 which shows her date of birth as 16.08.1965.
Accident took place on 23.01.2025.
She was aged 59 years at the time of accident.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner is considered as 59 years at the time of accident.
In respect of occupation it is stated that, she was Tailor by profession and was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
But, she has not produced any document to show her income.
Therefore notional income has to be considered.

Accident having taken place in the year 2025 the monthly income of the petitioner is held as Rs.17,000/-.
16.
In respect of permanent disability P.W.1 got examined Dr.Nagaraj B.N. as PW.3.
He is not a treated doctor.
He has assessed only disability.
According to him petitioner had sustained of right humerus middle third fracture with radial nerve Palsy and she underwent operation with implants in situ.

In his evidence he has mentioned that on examination of petitioner on 27.09.2025 for assessment of disability petitioner complaints of pain in right humerus, unable to lift weight and carry out her daily routine work as before.
P.W.3 doctor has assessed the permanent physical disability of right arm @45% and that of to the whole body disability @ 15%.

Petitioner having aged about 59 years and less chances of recovery from (SCCH-12) 10 MVC. No.1353/2025 grievous injury,
right hand being primary limb for any daily work to a woman, in the opinion of this court the functional disability affecting the income of the petitioner is 15%.

Hence the quantum of compensation is determined as under:
(i) Medical expenses:
The petitioner has produced 15 medical bills at Ex.P.12.
She has paid amount of Rs.1,84,450/- towards medical expenses.
Those bills are disputed but no concrete evidence is laid to dispute the bills.
Hence, petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,84,450/- under the head of medical expenses.

(ii) Food, nourishment, attendant and conveyance charges:

sentences.text: The petitioner underwent surgery to right humerus middle third fracture as per discharge summary produced at Ex.P.10.
It shows that petitioner was admitted for 4 days.
Considering the cost of living, food, nourishment, attendant and conveyance charges amount of Rs. 20,000/- is awarded.
(iii) Loss of income during laid up period: Minimum 3 months is required to recover from injury.
Hence, her loss of income during laid up period is considered as Rs.17,000 X 3 months Rs.51,000/-.
(iv) Loss of future income due to Disability:
As per the findings given above, there is 15% functional disability affecting the income of the petitioner.

Hence, loss of future income due to disability is Rs.17,000/-income X 12 months X 15% disability X 9 multiplier to the age group of 56 to 60 years which comes up to Rs.2,75,400/-
compensation is awarded under this head.
 (SCCH-12) 11 MVC. No.1353/2025 (v) For Future medical expenses:
As per the evidence of doctor there is need for future surgery for removal of implants but, no estimation is provided to that effect.
Hence amount of Rs.25,000/- is awarded for future medical treatment.
(vi) For Pain and sufferings:
As per Ex.P8 wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained "Fracture of right humerus with injury to radial nerve".
It is opined that said injury is grievous injury.
Therefore, towards pain and suffering the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/-.
(vii) Physical discomfort and loss of amenities of life: There is evidence of doctor to show that grievous injury has affected the normal life of the petitioner.

Therefore,
compensation of Rs.50,000/- is awarded under this head.

ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

It is held that, petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,81,265/- with interest @ 6% p.a on the amount of Rs.5,56,265/- from the date of petition till the date of payment.(Future medical expenses of Rs.25,000/- will not carry interest).

Respondent No.2 being insurer of vehicle is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner and hereby directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount with interest before this tribunal within 60 days from the date of this order.
On such deposit, the petitioner is entitled to have release of entire compensation amount without making FD.
The Advocate fee is fixed at  Rs.1,000/-.
Award be drawn accordingly.
